rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a reader holding only prior slides of THIS file hits a referent with no antecedent. Walked all 10 chunks. Chunk4/5 figure kickers establish 'kit' ('ONE ENGINEER'S KIT', 'A PUBLIC KIT · mattpocock/skills') before chunk7 L33 reuses it ('A kit skill can run on a schedule... a skill from your kit') and chunk9 L48 ('The field wires kits more ways than one') -- ordinary same-file reuse. Chunk8's figure (skill-sea-passage, same chunk as its bullets) labels 'one fix', 'carries one whole leg', 'at the pier' immediately above bullet L43's 'a single fix at a turning point... a whole leg... runs at the pier' -- same-chunk figure-to-bullet resolution, ok per rule text ('The chunk's own header counts as in-chunk'; figure sits in the same chunk). Chunk9 L48 names 'Pocock' and 'Klaassen' with no in-file gloss, but both are checked against the arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out: `curriculum/evals/arc-read.ae101.md:14` records a maintainer decision that 'all Klaassen encounters stay -- spine framework, he earns it. Don't re-flag'; Pocock is independently established two slides earlier at chunk5's own header+figure ('Pocock's skill system', 'A PUBLIC KIT · mattpocock/skills'). Chunk2 L11 'it' in 'The checks you built are the instruments inside it' resolves to 'the eval' bolded one bullet up in the same chunk. No never-named, vague-with-full-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

Harm prevented: a chunk locating content by its position in another file/module rather than naming what it is, which only resolves for a reader who already knows where that position sits. Chunk 7 'Loop instead of you starting' L34: 'a gap-finder reads the repo for the drift shape you saw at M5 and opens an issue when it finds one' -- 'at M5' is a bare module-ordinal locator, structurally identical to the rule's own banned example ('The opening lecture said...' -- which opener depends on where the deck starts), and unlike the rule's PASS example it does not unpack the claim in the same sentence (it says 'the drift shape', not which drift shape or what it looks like). This also contradicts the file's own maintainer accept-note at raw line 71: '**§3 disposition (no cross-module sequencing in body).** ... No `M[0-9]` tags in body.' Grepped the current body for `M[0-9]`: `grep -n 'M[0-9]' curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` restricted to lines 1-51 -> exactly one hit, line 34 ('M5'). The maintainer's own accept-note is describing a body that no longer matches the file (line 71 asserts zero M-tags; the body carries one). Rule 3 is separately satisfied -- 'goal drift' is a real, current M5 beat (`learn-from-the-test.md` L15-16 names 'goal drift' as one of three failure-mode lenses; `what-packaging-is.md` teaches drift extensively) -- so this is a naming-shape defect (rule 2), not a dead-reference defect (rule 3).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the drift shape inline instead of the module tag, e.g. 'the goal-drift shape you diagnosed against a live send-off' -- drops 'at M5' and unpacks the claim per the rule's own worked example. Also flags maintainer line 71's 'No M[0-9] tags in body' as no longer accurate (check_writing §3 territory, noted separately).
